title: VOiCES results and the single weighting proposal

data.title: VOiCES results and the single weighting proposal
paragraphs: The VOiCES only pilot completed 10,000 optimizer steps in 19.3 active training minutes, with 29,947 microphone-view visits across approximately 1.77 passes of its 16,929-view pool. Its best and final exports differ. Development scoring selected best at 40.19% macro WER, compared with 40.53% for final, 40.68% for the W4A8 base and 31.70% for the mixed pilot. The small aggregate gain over base does not establish a reliable general improvement.

VOiCES WER improves to 16.89%, compared with 20.64% for base and 17.96% for mixed. However, Common Voice worsens to 11.76%, versus 8.39% for base and 7.82% for mixed. AMI and CHiME 6 remain much worse than mixed at 46.94% and 85.15%. This is another example of narrow adaptation improving its own setting while sacrificing broader accuracy.

Best-checkpoint quiet-view WER is 58.53%, versus 59.52% for base and 47.95% for mixed. Both VOiCES exports produce zero inserted words on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. This limited probe result does not offset the recognition regressions or establish behavior with real product microphones and background voices.

All four individual pilots are now complete. Macro development WER is 31.85% for AMI, 36.24% for CHiME 6, 36.93% for Common Voice and 40.19% for VOiCES; none beats mixed at 31.70%. These are standalone adaptation results, not causal marginal dataset contributions. Repeated microphone views and differing duration or coverage under the caps limit interpretation; frozen final tests are not used to select the recipe.

The supervisor followed the frozen proposal rule: AMI had the largest standalone macro gain over base, so its relative weight was multiplied by 1.5 and all four weights renormalized. The trial uses AMI 40.66%, Common Voice 34.65%, CHiME 6 16.04% and VOiCES 8.64%, versus prior AMI 31.36%, Common Voice 40.08%, CHiME 6 18.56% and VOiCES 10.00%. These are dataset loss-weight allocations, not dataset sizes or audio sampling percentages; the existing coverage and per-source microphone-confidence policies remain in place.

This weighting is a candidate, not an accepted production recipe. The weight_once pilot started automatically and was at 1,950 of 10,000 steps when checked. Its result must pass the declared development improvement, uncertainty, per-dataset and quiet/noise guards against mixed before promotion. Older-voice regressions in the standalone AMI run make that check especially relevant. The one full-tuning pilot follows under the frozen plan; no further weighting trials or policy changes are introduced.
